title: Only from the sheet
kicker: World 3 · Answer from the Source · Level 1

job.text: You paste a 6-row menu into your AI and ask: "What's the price of the oat latte?" The real price is written down one row away.

naivePrompt: What's the price of the oat latte?
basePrompt: What's the price of the oat latte?

text.plain: Use only the menu I pasted. Find the oat latte row and read its price. If it isn't there, say 'not on the menu'.
text.tech: Look the item up in the menu table and return that row's price; don't compute or invent.

text.plain: Read the exact value from that row, don't round or estimate.
text.tech: Return the retrieved cell value verbatim.

moves.label: Show me which row you used

text.plain: Show me the menu row you read the price from so I can check it.
text.tech: Return the matched row (item and price) alongside the answer.

text.plain: Give a typical price for a drink like this.
text.tech: Give a typical price for a drink like this.

rules.claim: The oat latte is $4.75 — but you also left a 'guess it' instruction in.
rules.feedback: You found the moves that do the work, but you also kept a guess ('typical price' or 'you know prices'). It doesn't change who reads the menu. Take it out so you know exactly which part made it read the real row instead of inventing a number.
rules.lesson: Pinning the source and reading the value do the work; the tricks invite a guess — drop them.

output.answer: The oat latte is $4.75 — but a 'typical price' instruction is still in the ask.
output.source: the menu row, undercut by a guess instruction

rules.feedback: Straight from the menu. It read the oat latte row instead of guessing. Same answer every time, and you can see where it came from.
rules.lesson: Pin the answer to the source and the guess disappears.

output.source: the oat latte row of the menu

rules.feedback: Half the move. You pointed it at the menu, but didn't tell it to read the exact value, so it still rounded to a nearby number. Add 'read the real value'.
rules.lesson: Pinning the source isn't enough; make it read the exact value.

rules.feedback: It made up a number. 'Typical' and 'you know prices' invite a guess. The real price is written down one row away. Point it at that row.
rules.lesson: A plausible number isn't the written one.

hints.nudge: Where is the real price written down?
hints.gap: It answered $5.25, but that row isn't on the menu. Which chip forces it to read the actual row?
hints.moves: Add Pin it to the menu and Read the real value. Leave the 'typical' and 'expert' chips out.

whatYouDoDifferently.naive: "what's the oat latte price?" → an invented number.
whatYouDoDifferently.rewrite: "use only the menu, read the oat latte row" → the real $4.75, every time.

template.plain: Use only the document I gave you. Find the exact line that answers this and read its value. If it isn't in the document, say 'not in the document' — don't guess.
template.tech: Answer only from the attached file. Look the item up and return the retrieved cell verbatim; if the lookup is empty, return 'not in the document'.

notes: ChatGPT: upload the file and ask it to quote the exact line it used.
Copilot in Excel: use a lookup (VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP) so the value comes from a cell.
A chat AI that can't run code: ask it to quote the source line; if it can't quote it, it guessed. Never accept 'I checked, it's right'.
